evidence.limitations_of_proxies: Raw popularity indicators (GitHub stars, download counts) were recorded only as secondary, declared evidence alongside release-cadence and maintenance-policy evidence, consistent with the requirement that such raw counts not be used as a standalone proxy for the whole evaluation.
evidence.methodology_note: Predeclared domain/library sampling per Section 'Predeclared sampling'. Selection rule frozen before collection: for each application domain, the target library is (a) the artifact recommended/defaulted by the language's official or de-facto standard tooling (Spring Initializr defaults, JCP/JPA standardization), OR (b) the top-ranked artifact in that domain's category on mvnrepository.com/Maven Central popularity rankings. Candidate universe = mvnrepository.com category listings (Testing, Logging Frameworks, JSON Libraries, etc.) plus Maven Central search. Retrieval route = web search snapshot on 2026-09-22 against project GitHub release pages, official project sites, and Wikipedia infoboxes. Same retrieval depth (one web search pass per domain cluster) was used as declared for this worker's language-set.

metric.package_ecosystem_activity_mainte.rationale: All 6 independently re-verified flagship libraries (Spring Boot, Jackson, Hibernate ORM, JUnit, Logback, Guava) plus the core build tool (Maven) show recent releases within the last few months of the 2026-09-22 snapshot, active issue/milestone tracking, and in several cases concurrently maintained major-version lines (Jackson 2.x/3.x, Hibernate 6.x/7.x/8.0-dev, JUnit 5.x/6.x, Spring Boot 3.x EOL transition to 4.x). This indicates a highly active, well-maintained package ecosystem. Score is not 100 because EOL transitions were also observed (e.g., Spring Boot 3.5 reaching open-source end-of-life June 30, 2026), reflecting normal but real churn/maintenance-burden dynamics rather than uniformly indefinite support.

metric.third_party_library_availability_.rationale: 7 of 10 predeclared domains (web framework, JSON, ORM, testing, logging, general utility, build tooling) were independently verified this session to have canonical, actively maintained, Maven-Central-distributed libraries, several of which are spec-standardized (JPA/Hibernate) or de-facto standards bundled by default tooling (Spring Initializr, JUnit, Jackson). The remaining 3 domains (HTTP client, reactive, ML/numerical) are known by general knowledge to have mature or adequate coverage, with ML being the relatively weakest domain for the JVM ecosystem compared to Python. Score reflects near-complete domain coverage with a small deduction for the comparatively narrower ML/numerical-computing domain and for the 3 domains not independently re-verified with fresh citations this session.
